newsitem.title: USA: Mattel posts 15 percent higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mattel posts 15 percent higher earnings.

text.p: Toy maker Mattel Inc. reported an 11 percent increase in third-quarter profits Tuesday, attributing the rise to "excellent retail demand" and strong performances by its Barbie, Hot Wheels and Cabbage Patch Kids products.
The No.1 U.S. toy manufacturer posted $168 million in net income, or 61 cents per share, vs. net income of $151 million, or 53 cents per share, in last year's third quarter.
Earnings exceeded the consensus prediction of 59 cents per share, according to the First Call service, which tracks analyst estimates.
El Segundo, Calif.-based Mattel generated revenues of $1.232 billion, a 5 percent increase from year-ago revenues of $1.176 billion.
Mattel stock rose $1.125 to $26.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Our momentum continues to build as we approach the prime holiday selling season," Mattel Chairman John Amerman said in a statement. "Excellent retail demand for our products gives us confidence in our outlook for the full year."
Amerman said the company's Hot Wheels cars and Barbie and Cabbage Patch Kids dolls were performing well in the marketplace.

"With our strongest 1996 new product introductions now reaching retail shelves and our plans for aggressive advertising and promotion support, we are on track to achieve excellent fourth-quarter performance," he said.
The company also said its board had approved the expansion of a stock buyback programme, from 8.75 million shares to 10 million shares.
Mattel has offices and other facilities in 36 countries and sells its products in 140 nations.
